conflicts.point: The viability and appropriateness of applying physical hardware tracking models to digital software weights.

positions.stance: Argues that tracking high-end hardware and setting compute floors provides an effective choke point analogous to nuclear and chemical supply chain controls.
Maintains that model weights are infinitely duplicable digital matrices rather than scarce physical substances, rendering physical supply chain controls ineffective.

conflicts.point: Whether static computational thresholds can remain effective given rapid algorithmic efficiency gains.

positions.stance: Maintains that fixed compute thresholds like 10^25 FLOPs can reliably separate high-risk enterprise training runs from university and open-weight experimentation.
Argues that rapid algorithmic efficiency compression halves required compute every year, turning enterprise thresholds into undergraduate cluster ceilings within three years.
